**The Poem of a Thousand Words**

I wrote one word,
then another—
a river of ink
flowing gently,
filling the page
the way time fills
a dead man’s lungs.

I wrote *ghost* next,
then *moon*,
then *the way*
the telephone rings
at 3 AM,
then *the way*
a name can feel
like a foreign
country’s wind.

I wrote *I am*
and *I am not*
and *I am*
still not sure
which one
is the truth.

I wrote *silence*
the way you write
your name in sand—
knowing the tide
will come for it.

I wrote *God*
like a child
scribbling
on a church pew.
I wrote *blood*
like a thief
stealing
from the altar.

I wrote *time*
and *teeth*
and *the way*
a heart can crack
like a frozen lake
under too much
weight.
I wrote *forgive me*
in every language
I’ve ever known.

I wrote *I miss*
but left no object,
no person,
no ghost—
just the hollow
where the word
should have been.

I wrote *light*
like a child
holding a match
to the dark.
I wrote *ash*
like a man
writing the names
of the dead
on his own skin.

I wrote *you*
and then I wrote
*sometimes*
and then I wrote
*maybe*
and then I wrote
*nothing at all*
just the space
between my fingers
and the page.

I wrote *goodbye*
the way you say
it to a lover
you know
will never leave.

I wrote *love*
like a gambler
betting his last
chip on a horse
that might not come
in.

I wrote *enough*
but it tasted
like salt
on my lips.

I wrote *forever*
and then I wrote
*never*
and then I wrote
*how strange*
that both
could fit
in the same mouth.

I wrote *I tried*
and then I wrote
*I failed*
and then I wrote
*I am sorry*
to the world
and its cracked
mirrors.

I wrote *nothing*
until the nothing
wrote me back.

Now the page
is full.
The ink is dry.
The words
are just holes
where light
used to be.
